mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals restrictive monetary policy that depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 2 months) (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong labor market growth (PAYEMS > 100k monthly) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) indicates robust economic conditions that drive positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where PAYEMS > 100k and UNRATE < 4.0% (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, rising housing starts (HOUST > 1500k) and strong GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized) signal sustained consumer demand, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods meeting the late-cycle expansion regime and HOUST > 1500k with GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in industrial production (INDPRO increasing for 3 consecutive months) indicates strengthening supply capacity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with INDPRO increasing for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, it reflects a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances (UNRATE < 4.0% for 2 months) (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) combined with elevated interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) creates a stagflationary environment that reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods with CPIAUCSL > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4.0% (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: During supply shocks, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100) and falling housing starts (HOUST < 1400k) indicate reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the supply shock regime (INDPRO < 100 and HOUST < 1400k) (t-test p > 0.05 vs. baseline).
